label: Markdown
headline: Markdown Cheat Sheet
description: Quick reference for Markdown — headings, emphasis, lists, links, images, tables, code blocks, and more. Works in GitHub, Notion, VS Code, and anywhere Markdown is rendered.

items.name: H1
items.definition: Top-level heading. There should typically be only one H1 per document.

items.name: H2
items.definition: Second-level heading — used for major sections.

items.name: H3
items.definition: Third-level heading — used for sub-sections.

items.name: H4 – H6
items.definition: Deeper heading levels using 4, 5, or 6 hash symbols.

items.name: Setext H1
items.definition: Alternate H1 syntax using a line of = signs beneath the text.

items.name: Setext H2
items.definition: Alternate H2 syntax using a line of - signs beneath the text.

items.name: Bold
items.definition: Wrap text in double asterisks or double underscores (__bold__) for bold.

items.name: Italic
items.definition: Wrap text in single asterisks or single underscores (_italic_) for italic.

items.name: Bold + Italic
items.definition: Triple asterisks (or underscores) for combined bold and italic emphasis.

items.name: Strikethrough
items.definition: Wrap text in double tildes to render with a strikethrough line. (GFM extension)

items.name: Inline code
items.definition: Wrap text in backticks to render as monospaced code inline.

items.name: Highlight
items.definition: Some renderers (like Obsidian) support == for highlighted text.

items.name: Unordered list
items.definition: Use -, *, or + as bullet markers. All three are interchangeable.

items.name: Ordered list
items.definition: Number followed by a period. Numbers don't need to be sequential — the renderer counts them.

items.name: Nested list
items.syntax:
- Item 1
  - Sub-item A
  - Sub-item B
- Item 2
items.definition: Indent sub-items by 2–4 spaces (or one tab) to create nesting.

items.name: Task / checkbox
items.definition: GitHub Flavored Markdown (GFM) renders these as interactive checkboxes. x = checked.

items.name: Inline link
items.definition: Square brackets hold the display text, parentheses hold the URL.

items.name: Link with title
items.definition: Add a quoted title inside the parentheses to show a tooltip on hover.

items.name: Reference link
items.definition: Define the URL separately using a label. Keeps the text clean for long URLs used multiple times.

items.name: Bare URL
items.definition: Angle brackets auto-link a URL. Also works for email: <user@example.com>.

items.name: Anchor link
items.definition: Link to a heading within the same document. Headings become anchors (lowercase, hyphens for spaces).

items.name: Basic image
items.definition: Same as a link but with a ! prefix. Alt text improves accessibility and SEO.

items.name: Image with title
items.definition: Adds a tooltip title that appears on hover.

items.name: Reference image
items.definition: Define the image URL separately using a reference label.

items.name: Linked image
items.definition: Wrap an image in a link by nesting the image syntax inside link brackets.

items.name: Inline code
items.definition: Single backticks render code inline with monospaced font.

items.name: Fenced code block
items.definition: Triple backticks create a code block. Add a language identifier for syntax highlighting.

items.name: Tilde fence
items.definition: Alternative to backtick fencing. Useful when your code contains backticks.

items.name: Indented code block
items.definition: Indent each line by 4 spaces or 1 tab. Works in basic Markdown without backticks.

items.name: Basic blockquote
items.definition: Prefix lines with > to create a blockquote.

items.name: Multi-line
items.syntax:
> Line one
> Line two
> Line three
items.definition: Prefix each line with > for a multi-line blockquote.

items.name: Nested blockquote
items.definition: Use >> (with a blank > line between) to nest blockquotes.

items.name: Blockquote with content
items.definition: Blockquotes can contain other Markdown elements like headings and lists.

items.name: Basic table
items.definition: GFM tables: headers in the first row, a separator row of dashes, then data rows. Pipes separate columns.

items.name: Left align
items.definition: Colon on the left of the separator dashes aligns the column to the left.

items.name: Center align
items.definition: Colons on both sides of the dashes centers the column.

items.name: Right align
items.definition: Colon on the right of the dashes aligns the column to the right.

items.name: Dashes
items.definition: Three or more dashes on their own line produce a horizontal divider rule.

items.name: Asterisks
items.definition: Three or more asterisks also produce a horizontal rule.

items.name: Underscores
items.definition: Three or more underscores produce a horizontal rule.

items.name: Escape character
items.definition: Prefix a Markdown character with \ to display it literally.

items.name: Escapable chars
items.definition: These characters have special meaning in Markdown. Escape them with \ when you want the literal symbol.

items.name: Line break
items.definition: End a line with two or more spaces, then press Enter to insert a hard line break (\<br\>).

items.name: Comment (HTML)
items.definition: Markdown supports HTML comments. They are not rendered in the output.

items.name: HTML inline
items.definition: Raw HTML is supported in most Markdown renderers. Useful for features Markdown doesn't natively support.

items.name: Paragraph break
items.definition: A blank line between text creates a new paragraph.

items.name: Strikethrough
items.definition: GitHub Flavored Markdown (GFM) renders double tildes as strikethrough text.

items.name: Task list
items.definition: Interactive checkboxes in GitHub pull requests, issues, and wikis.

items.name: Footnote
items.definition: Some renderers (GitHub, Obsidian) support footnotes with a [^label] syntax.

items.name: Definition list
items.definition: Supported in some Markdown flavors (MultiMarkdown, Pandoc) — not standard GFM.

items.name: Emoji
items.definition: GitHub and many other renderers support emoji shortcodes wrapped in colons.

items.name: Auto-link
items.definition: GFM auto-links URLs that start with http://, https://, or www. without needing angle brackets.
